newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares gain in modest Western buying.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares gain in modest Western buying.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed as Western buyers cautiously edged into the market on Friday, traders said, seeing levels steady at the start of next week.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index rose 1.42 percent to 563.14 from 555.23 on Thursday on a robust market share turnover of $81.2 million.
National power company UES closed up at $0.4495 on the RTS after $0.4425 at the previous close while metals producer Norilsk Nickel eased to $16.25 from $16.65.
CentreInvest Securities sales director Dan Rapoport said Western interest had crept up after several days of wandering interest and drifting prices.

"It looks like the West has picked up the pace -- some investors have gotten used to the new prices and decided to go in and start cautiously buying," Rapoport said. "They're not bidding outrageous prices. They're careful in what they select."

Rapoport said he saw profit taking in utilities and telecom companies which had risen several weeks ago, but said foreign investors were buying smaller oil companies, refineries and metal plants among less liquid shares on the second tier RTS.
Aton trader Boris Shvedsky said the market was likely to stay buoyant next week on small fund flows and Russian interest.
Traders saw the market as unchanged or gaining modestly.

"Banks and local investors were big contributors to the rise today and it wasn't that much of a rise anyway," said Creditanstalt Grant director of sales Tad Berger. "Next week I wouldn't expect anything too much either way."
